merge_hypotheses.description: If critical acclaim, public legitimacy, and perceived Academy comfort align, both skeptical and enthusiastic timelines converge toward Album B as a plausible consensus winner.
Divergent public narratives may still converge in uncertainty because secret balloting hides true coalition strength until the result.
Regardless of side narratives, all paths converge on the same terminal evidence standard: official Album of the Year result only.

simulation_brief.summary: A global Latin artist's Spanish-language Album B is nominated for the 2026 Grammy Awards Album of the Year. The album has strong critical prominence and commercial visibility, with milestone narrative momentum, but faces historical headwinds in a category that has often favored English-language releases and broad Recording Academy consensus. Multiple major English-language pop, rap, and singer-songwriter nominees create a competitive field. Terminal resolution is strictly whether Album B wins the official Album of the Year category.
simulation_brief.decision_context: Single terminal decision by Recording Academy voters on official Album of the Year award outcome.
uncertainty_notes: Specific nominee identities beyond Album B are masked or not provided.
Voting body composition and campaign details are not fully specified.
No explicit evidence at T0 of scandal, disqualification, or vote split mechanics beyond general competition.

branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Album B remains a celebrated nominee but loses final consensus to an English-language competitor.
branch_hypotheses.divergence_signal: Forecast discourse converges on precedent, broad appeal, and category fit as decisive over novelty.

branch_hypotheses.trigger: No single English-language nominee consolidates clear frontrunner status among pop, rap, and singer-songwriter lanes.
branch_hypotheses.alternate_path: Fragmentation among rivals allows Album B to win with a pluralistic coalition.
